commitments.claim: Raising expected FY26 AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers to $9 billion (from $5 billion) and related FY26 AI revenue to $4 billion (from $3 billion)
Major multi-year multi-billion-dollar campus networking refresh underway; campus orders >25% Y/Y and next-gen portfolio ramping faster than prior launches; data center switching orders >40% Y/Y
Restructuring plan up to $1B pre-tax (severance and related) to fund silicon, optics, security and AI; ~$450M in Q4 FY26 and remainder in FY27

Q4 FY26 non-GAAP operating margin guided 34–35% and non-GAAP gross margin 65.5–66.5% including tariff impact; capital return via ~$0.42 dividend and ongoing buybacks ($9.6B authorization remaining at Q3)

buy_triggers.marker: Q4 FY2026 product orders growth still ≥25% Y/Y with AI infra orders run-rate supporting ≥$5B FY27 AI revenue contribution
Non-GAAP operating margin ≥34.5% in Q4 and FY27 Q1 with GAAP gross margin stabilizing ≥63.5% despite hyperscaler mix
FY2027 revenue guide issued ≥$66.5B and non-GAAP EPS guide ≥$4.55 on the Q4 call
FCF (CFO+capex) trailing twelve months ≥$14B with buybacks+dividends sustained ≥$11B annualized

sell_triggers.marker: Networking product revenue growth decelerates to <10% Y/Y for two consecutive quarters

thesis.what_must_be_true: Cisco converts elevated networking and AI-infra orders into mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth through FY27–28 while holding non-GAAP op margin near 34–35% after the FY26/27 restructuring reinvestment; campus refresh and silicon/optics attach must offset services softness and tariff/mix pressure so that FCF stays above $14B and capital return remains intact.

validated.preview_note: CSCO prints FY26 Q4 after a blowout Q3 ($15.8B, +12% Y/Y) that cleared the high end, with product orders +35% (+19% ex-hyperscalers), networking +50%+, and AI-infra orders raised to $9B / revenue to $4B for FY26. Street setup is the raised $16.7–16.9B / $1.16–1.18 non-GAAP EPS guide plus ~$450M restructuring. Three swing factors: (1) how much AI and campus order strength converts in-quarter vs. builds backlog—mix may clip GAAP GM toward low-64% but volume can push revenue through the high end; (2) whether non-GAAP OM lands 34.5%+ after the charge (add-back); (3) initial FY27 framework and any further AI order color. Beat-and-raise on FY27 growth with stable mid-34% OM should be rewarded; in-line revenue with GM miss or soft FY27 guide risks a de-rate given how far orders have run.
validated.reasoning: Anchored on Q3 FY26 as-filed 8-K/10-Q (rev 15841, NI 3373, EPS 0.85, non-GAAP EPS 1.06, cash 7083, RE 704, 9M rev 46073) and company Q4/FY guides (rev 16.7–16.9 / 62.8–63.0; non-GAAP EPS 1.16–1.18 / 4.27–4.29; ~$450M Q4 restructuring). Q3 cleared guide high by ~$0.2–0.4B on 35% order growth and raised AI targets, so I place Q4 rev p50 at 17020 (above guide high) and non-GAAP EPS p50 at 1.175 (upper half of guide) with GAAP EPS 0.83 after $450M restructuring. GAAP GM ~63.8% (hyperscaler mix/tariffs); opex scaled for growth plus restructuring; tax ~16% GAAP. Bridge mirrors Q3 architecture (SBC, intangibles amort, acq costs, restructuring, investment gains, tax). CFO ~4.1B with still-elevated inventory/WC; capex -450; FCF 3685; buybacks/dividends in line with Q3 run-rate. BS rolls cash 7083-581=6502 and RE 704+3296-1668-1250=1082. FY0 = 9M+Q4. FY27 path assumes ~7–8% growth as AI revenue annualizes and campus refresh continues, margins stable mid-34% OM, FCF expands as WC normalizes and restructuring savings land. Guidance_forecast for Q1 FY27 is seasonally off Q4 peak but up Y/Y. Risks: tariff escalation, hyperscaler concentration, services flatness; upside if silicon/optics attach and security re-accelerate.
